claims.text: Structural and chemical stability of multi-element, near-equiatomic solid-solution nanoparticles at high temperature is governed by fabrication optimization integrating experimental characterization and simulation-based modeling.
Combining experimental characterization with simulation-based modeling can identify the key factors controlling nanoparticle stability.
The proposed optimization produces an optimized nanoparticle composition and microstructure.
Identifying stability-controlling factors enables fabrication approaches to be optimized.
Optimized fabrication produces nanoparticles with improved structural stability at high temperature.
Optimized fabrication produces nanoparticles with improved chemical stability at high temperature.
Improved structural and chemical stability enhances catalytic performance.
Improved structural and chemical stability enhances thermoelectric performance.
The relevant catalytic service-temperature range is 773–1173 K.
The relevant thermoelectric service-temperature range is 473–1923 K.
Conventionally fabricated nanoparticles without optimization constitute the baseline.
The exact relationship among nanoparticle composition, microstructure, and high-temperature stability remains uncertain.
Optimized nanoparticles are predicted to show greater structural and chemical stability than conventionally fabricated nanoparticles.
Optimized nanoparticles are predicted to show better catalytic and thermoelectric performance than conventionally fabricated nanoparticles.
